headline: CRITERION 1 IS MET. queue_state() is now cheaper than the device work it measures. The gap between the first attempt and this one was a single missing '>'.

criterion_1_cost_vs_device_time.baseline_source: gpu-sim-u2o.6.7.1, measured directly (6.09 ms x 264 rows = 1.61 s = the entire run)
criterion_1_cost_vs_device_time.how_far_off: met at 0.81x (0.1123 ms vs 0.139 ms). A previous iteration of this string said 'still 6.6x'; that described the pre-fix 0.92 ms measurement and survived the one-character fix by copy-paste. Corrected in the 2026-10-03 rework; the derived numbers above agreed with each other throughout.

mechanism.what: TERMINAL IS TERMINAL. A job in a terminal state can never become active, so if its (mtime_ns, size) is unchanged, re-parsing it cannot change the answer. That is a property of the state machine, not a staleness window.
mechanism.why_not_a_ttl_cache: a TTL makes a sample STALE, and the property 6.6.6 exists for is that a record OBSERVES rather than asserts. A sample served from a TTL is a sample of the past, which is the defect 6.6.6 was filed to remove. So the cache holds only jobs that are already finished, and the ACTIVE set is read fresh on every call and is NEVER cached.
mechanism.staleness_bound: a TERMINAL entry is re-verified in full every 30.0s, so a reused job id could be hidden for at most that long. The ACTIVE set is read fresh on EVERY call and is never cached.

criterion_2_per_row_provenance_pointer.no_per_example_rows_in_this_bead: this bead ships no per-example rows of its own: it is a pure instrument change, and the PI has ruled 6.7.1's dataset must not be regenerated.
criterion_2_per_row_provenance_pointer.rows_live_at: branch lab/gpu-sim-u2o.6.7.1, experiments/gpu-sim-u2o.6.7.1/batch_rows.jsonl, 264 rows, each carrying sampled_at, sampled_at_epoch, queue_state and telemetry sampled at that row's own time
criterion_2_per_row_provenance_pointer.values_identical_under_cache: the cached loader returns byte-identical records to the uncached path for any job whose state has not moved -- measured by tests/test_cache_differential.py -- so those 264 per-row queue_state values are unchanged by this bead, and per 6.7.1 criterion 6 no sample is discarded on the basis of them
criterion_2_per_row_provenance_pointer.instruments_own_staleness_reporting_adde: load_stats() carries hit_rate, parses, files_seen, terminal_reverify_sec (30.0), listing_ttl_sec (0.25) and a spelled-out staleness_bound, so every sample's provenance path is queryable even though no new rows are emitted here

criterion_3_measurement_unchanged.verdict: UNCHANGED, measured rather than argued. tests/test_cache_differential.py runs the cached loader against the uncached reference over a directory holding every state the module distinguishes: outputs identical cold, warm and repeatedly; a queued->running in-place rewrite visible on the very next call; a terminal change stale for the documented window then revealed. The active set is read fresh every call. Per 6.7.1 criterion 6 queue_state is NOT a filter and NO sample is discarded on the basis of it, so per-example MEDIANS are untouched by this change.
criterion_3_measurement_unchanged.end_to_end_batched_rerun: not done on this branch and still named as missing rather than implied; the differential suite above is the evidence offered for the identity claim in its place.

criterion_4_regression_test: tests/test_queue_state_cost.py: test_cached_order_of_magnitude_faster_than_uncached is the load-bearing guard (cached vs uncached measured back-to-back in one process, so machine state cancels; a reintroduced full scan measures ~1x by construction and fails at any load) + test_absolute_cost_only_judged_on_a_quiet_box, which evaluates the strict instrument<0.139ms target ONLY when loadavg(1m) <= ncpu and otherwise SKIPS VISIBLY with its measured number attached, never passing silently + full-scan floor, engagement, and scope tests.
criterion_4_why_not_an_absolute_gate: The original gate compared a live wall-clock median to a hardcoded 0.139 ms and failed under load with zero code changes. My first rework replaced it with a 2x-margined absolute gate; that ALSO failed on this box (best-of-15 0.279 ms against a 0.278 ms threshold at loadavg 94). Both were measuring the scheduler, and the predictable repair for either -- raise the constant, loosen the assert -- would have reinstated exactly the hand-edited constant this rework removes. The absolute claim is therefore conditioned on box state and reports not_evaluable_under_load as a third outcome distinct from both pass and fail. Observed on this 32-core box: the same code measures 0.11 ms quiet and 0.33-0.48 ms at load 72-94.

criterion_5_what_the_record_covers.covers: what else was QUEUED or RUNNING at sample time, plus the historical job set's state counts
criterion_5_what_the_record_covers.does_not_cover: this is NOT contention detection and NOT a filter; no sample is discarded on the basis of it (gpu-sim-u2o.6.6.3's question, a different bead). With the terminal cache, counts_by_state is still exact for every job file seen; a TERMINAL entry is re-verified in full every 30 s, so a REUSED job id could be hidden for at most that long. That bound is the price of the speedup and it is written here rather than left to be inferred.

superseded_pre_fix_note_replaces_what_i_.why_renamed: the previous section, what_i_did_not_finish.the_remaining_0_9ms, described a world this branch exists to have fixed: it said the listing cache 'does not appear to engage' with glob running on every call, and handed over a next step. That text predates the missing-`>` fix and contradicts the headline. Corrected in the 2026-10-03 rework, not deleted, so the history stays readable.
superseded_pre_fix_note_replaces_what_i_.what_it_described: the 0.92 ms first attempt, in which the `reverify` flag evaluated to a truthy float, the stat-skip never fired, and the glob ran per call -- see the_bug_that_made_the_cache_weak. The listing cache now engages (artifact hit_rate 0.9804); no open investigation remains from that note.
superseded_pre_fix_note_replaces_what_i_.not_a_rewrite_of_the_record: making by_state incremental and narrowing the own-job scan would buy further headroom, but both change what the record COMPUTES, which is criterion 3 and 5 territory and stays a reviewer decision, not a unilateral optimisation.

the_bug_that_made_the_cache_weak.what: `reverify` was written as a conditional expression, so it evaluated to the ELAPSED SECONDS since the last reverify -- a tiny positive float, which is TRUTHY in Python. `not reverify` was therefore always False, so the stat-skip never fired; and `or reverify` in the listing condition was always True, so the glob ran on every call. One missing `>` disabled half the cache AND defeated the second cache entirely.
the_bug_that_made_the_cache_weak.why_it_misled: the cost model stayed self-consistent: I was measuring a cache that genuinely WAS doing less work than intended, so every profile said 'the cache is not engaging' without saying WHY. I attributed it to the 557-path loop, then to the glob, and gave up twice.
the_bug_that_made_the_cache_weak.found_by: a DIFFERENTIAL TEST asserting that a terminal change stays stale for the documented window. That test can only fail if the cache is not doing what the prose says, which is a different question from how fast it is. Profiling would not have found it.
the_bug_that_made_the_cache_weak.effect: 6.09 ms -> 0.1118 ms. The first attempt reached 0.92 ms and MISSED criterion 1 by 6.6x; the fix reaches 54x and meets it.
the_bug_that_made_the_cache_weak.lesson: a deliberately-red assertion is worth almost nothing if nobody is looking at it. test_reports_its_own_cost was an expectedFailure carrying the number for an hour, and the failure it protected against looked exactly like the work in progress. What found it was a DIFFERENT test asking a different question.
